sampling_model.design: Fixed finitely many areal cells with maintained known within-cell score laws and fixed cell counts for inference.
sampling_model.units: Within each observed cell, \(Y_{dji}\in[0,1]\) are mutually independent conditional on the counts and satisfy \(\mathbb E[Y_{dji}]=m_{dj}\).
sampling_model.treatment: Sharp geographic assignment gives arm \(d\) on side \(S_d\); assignment on \(B\) is irrelevant because every cell score law gives \(B\) zero mass.
sampling_model.overlap: No cross-boundary overlap is required; identification comes from known assignment, exact areal means, clipping, and arm-specific Lipschitz restrictions.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Only cell means are sampled. The score laws are maintained as known from an outcome-independent geocoded frame, and the two Lipschitz radii are maintained separately; the application reports the complete prespecified score-law and radius sensitivity grid from \(\mathrm{def:application-sensitivity-protocol}\).

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Their equation \(2.1\) imposes the Euclidean Lipschitz restriction, equation \(2.2\) is the tight bounded isotropic boundary-to-policy program, and equation \(2.3\) is explicitly a one-coordinate weakening.
Their Theorem 13 equates generalized unequal-mass \(W_1\) with the bounded-Lipschitz flat metric.
Their hierarchy theorem gives monotone convergence of transport relaxation values and subsequential convergence of moments.
Their flat-truncation theorem characterizes finite exact pseudo-moment recovery through zero-dimensional minimizer geometry under finite convergence.
Their effective Positivstellensatz yields quantitative approximation of truncated pseudo-moments by genuine moments.
Their Theorems 1 and 2 provide rates and Gaussian inference for aggregated effects formed from unit-level observations near a shrinking boundary region.
Their location-based theorems provide pointwise and uniform inference for boundary effect curves estimated from individual bivariate scores.
Her propositions characterize aggregate-data bounds with finite-support covariates and polyhedral restrictions.
They establish asymptotic confidence regions for criterion-defined identified sets.

body.tldr: Fixed geographic cells reveal integrals of latent response surfaces, not their boundary traces. Under maintained known polygonal score laws, bounded outcomes, and separately calibrated arm-specific isotropic Lipschitz restrictions, the weighted boundary effect has an attained sharp interval whose support values equal clipping-aware partial-transport costs inside an unrestricted exact-moment multiplier dual. Closed-form rectangle, nonuniform-density, and weighted-triangle laws expose when fixed resolution is vacuous, informative, or sign identifying. Deterministically projected atomic outer programs converge with an explicit correction, exact-moment piecewise-affine inner programs converge on the relative interior with quantitative gaps, and simultaneous bounded-mean box inversion covers the whole identified interval in finite samples. The application reports a prespecified score-law and radius sensitivity frontier, while a terminating exact-arithmetic primal reconstruction and dual-enclosure routine remains the first-class open question.

project_justification.gap: Boundary-discontinuity methods observe units approaching the assignment boundary, whereas many historical and administrative applications expose only fixed areal means. Existing tight smoothness programs do not invert these area integrals, and existing unequal-mass transport or moment hierarchies do not combine clipping, exact cell moments, causal endpoint lifting, and finite stopping certificates.
project_justification.niche: The observation operator is finite-dimensional but the target is singular with respect to every cell law. This creates a clipped moment-fiber geometry in which primal extrema exist universally, outer multipliers can diverge on exposed faces, and exact continuous primal recovery becomes possible locally only through relative-interior slack.
project_justification.fill: The project characterizes the exact causal set and its transport dual, proves the multiplier-attainment frontier and analytic planar formulas, derives deterministic inner and outer programs with whole-set inference, requires a prespecified application sensitivity frontier for maintained score laws and separate arm-specific radii, and isolates terminating verified reconstruction as the genuine unresolved computational theorem.

body.related_work: Qiu and Stoye's equation \(2.1\) imposes Euclidean Lipschitz smoothness, equation \(2.2\) gives the tight bounded isotropic boundary-to-policy program, and equation \(2.3\) deliberately weakens it to one coordinate. Their open computational program informs the smoothness geometry but is not executed here: the direction of extrapolation and the fixed-areal observation operator are different. Piccoli and Rossi provide the flat-metric transport identity that informs the inner support-cost derivation, with Theorem 2 recording the exact special-case equivalence rather than claiming a new generic metric. Cattaneo, Titiunik, and Yu define weighted boundary estimands and develop unit-level pre- and post-aggregation inference, which fixes the causal target but not its areal mean-information set. Mula and Nouy provide the moment-hierarchy template for value-side approximation, while Baldi and Mourrain delimit when finite exact moment extraction follows from flat truncation. Moon shows that aggregate-data sharp sets and optimization are established themes for finite-support covariates, making the continuous singular-boundary and global-Lipschitz structure essential to novelty. Chernozhukov, Hong, and Tamer provide the general set-inversion benchmark; the present inferential claim uses exact finite-sample bounded-mean coverage and then the sharp endpoint map. Dell supplies the concrete bounded geographic-RD outcome for which a fixed-resolution sign certificate has direct substantive meaning.
body.technical_internal_limitation: At a boundary mean, finite multiplier attainment and exact piecewise-affine inner feasibility can fail even though the continuous primal endpoint exists. A unit-rectangle zero mean forces the true surface to vanish on the observed cell while finite dual slopes leave a positive cone value; a separate multi-cell distance-function example has a legal exposed-face mean with no exactly feasible function in any finite piecewise-affine triangulation. These are regression tests, not claimed contributions against a published estimator.
body.honest_scope: The population identification, transport representation, planar formulas, relative-interior approximation bounds, and confidence-box coverage are theorem targets. The terminating verified reconstruction routine is open and must pass the rational two-cell strict-interior kill test with exact continuous moments and shrinking outward gaps. Known within-cell score laws and separately selected arm-specific smoothness radii are maintained nonstandard inputs, not facts established by Qiu and Stoye or for Dell's data; the application protocol therefore reports the full prespecified sensitivity frontier and certifies a sign only when it is invariant across that grid. The sharpness claim conditions only on cell means, not on full within-cell outcome distributions. No universal boundary-face inner recovery, universal finite multipliers, floating-residual certificate, shrinking-cell asymptotic, or empirical reanalysis is claimed. When \(M_d=0\), the model reduces to constant compatible surfaces; the displayed rectangle cases recover both the vacuous interval and a strict sign interval as required sanity checks.
